article_title: Assessment of Knowledge of Acute Kidney Injury among Non-Nephrology Doctors in Two Government Hospitals in Ondo City, Southwest, Nigeria.
citation: Adejumo Oluseyi, Akinbodewa Ayodeji, Alli Oladimeji, Olufemi Pirisola, Olatunji Abolarin. (2017). Assessment of Knowledge of Acute Kidney Injury among Non-Nephrology Doctors in Two Government Hospitals in Ondo City, Southwest, Nigeria. Ethiopian Journal of Health Sciences. https://doi.org/10.4314/ejhs.v27i2.7
title: 32-item validated AKI knowledge questionnaire with scoring bands
description: A closed-ended structured questionnaire of 32 questions assessing AKI knowledge across clinical features, types, risk factors, nephrotoxic medications, diagnosis and staging criteria, newer biomarkers and renal replacement therapy indications. It was piloted with 20 non-nephrology doctors at State Specialist Hospital Akure, and "The Cronbach's alpha internal consistency coefficient of the questionnaire was 0.72". Each correct answer scores 1 point (maximum 32), with 24–32 good, 16–23 fair and <16 poor knowledge.
requirements: Administered as a self-administered pretested questionnaire to non-nephrology doctors; scoring uses the printed 24–32 / 16–23 / <16 bands
constraints: The instrument was validated in a pilot with 20 respondents in a different hospital and the authors note the main study's small sample limits generalisability
target_learning_goals: assessing knowledge of acute kidney injury prevention, diagnosis and management
examples: Used in the Ondo City cross-sectional survey of 81 doctors between April and May 2016 with a 90% response rate
key_sources: Adejumo Oluseyi, Akinbodewa Ayodeji, Alli Oladimeji, Olufemi Pirisola, Olatunji Abolarin. (2017). Assessment of Knowledge of Acute Kidney Injury among Non-Nephrology Doctors in Two Government Hospitals in Ondo City, Southwest, Nigeria. Ethiopian Journal of Health Sciences. https://doi.org/10.4314/ejhs.v27i2.7

article_title: Enhancing Essay Cohesion Assessment: A Novel Item Response Theory Approach
citation: Bruno Alexandre Rosa, Hilário Oliveira, Luiz Rodrigues, Eduardo Araujo Oliveira, Rafael Ferreira Mello. (2025). Enhancing Essay Cohesion Assessment: A Novel Item Response Theory Approach. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08487v1
title: 325-feature linguistic feature set for Portuguese essay cohesion prediction, grouped into 13 categories
description: The study extracted a comprehensive set of language-independent features to transform essays into numerical vectors for regression models. As the article states, "Table 2 summarises the 325 linguistic features used in this study", and "the features were grouped into 13 categories" including Coh-Metrix (87 features), LIWC (64), Word Morphsyn Information (39), Connectives (33), Semantic Cohesion, Lexical Diversity, Syntactic Complexity, Descriptive Measures, Referential Cohesion, Textual Simplicity, Sequential Cohesion, Readability, and Syntactic Patterns Density. The selection was informed by prior research on essay evaluation and cohesion assessment.
requirements: Portuguese-language resources including the Portuguese version of Coh-Metrix and the Portuguese LIWC 2007 dictionary
target_learners: secondary and upper-secondary students writing Portuguese essays
target_learning_goals: feature-based prediction of textual cohesion scores in educational essays
examples: Coh-Metrix contributed 87 descriptors (26.77% of features) and LIWC 64 categories from a lexicon of 127,149 words
key_sources: Bruno Alexandre Rosa, Hilário Oliveira, Luiz Rodrigues, Eduardo Araujo Oliveira, Rafael Ferreira Mello. (2025). Enhancing Essay Cohesion Assessment: A Novel Item Response Theory Approach. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08487
